newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba lowers cigarette prices to boost sales.
newsitem.headline: Cuba lowers cigarette prices to boost sales.

text.p: Cuba on Tuesday lowered the price of non-rationed cigarettes in a move aimed at boosting sales and revenue for the state.

The price drop was announced in the ruling Communist Party daily Granma, which added that the government in no way wished to encourage excessive consumption of tobacco. The logic of the move lies in a complex state distribution system that divides cigarette sales into cheap, rationed sales and non-rationed "free" sales, which are more expensive.

Rationed tobacco is allocated monthly for 7.8 million of Cuba's population of 11 million at two pesos and 2.50 pesos respectively for a pack of 20 dark tobacco and blonde tobacco cigarettes. Since only about four million people smoke, non-smokers and state store owners traditionally earn a little extra with resales on the street of rationed tobacco, undercutting sales of "free" tobacco.

With Tuesday's move, the price of dark cigarettes fell from 10 pesos a pack to seven while a pack of blonde tobacco dropped from 10.50 pesos to 7.60. The peso is currently worth $0.05 and an average worker in Cuba earns about 150-200 pesos a month.

Tuesday's cut in the price of non-rationed tobacco was accompanied by an announcement that some ration entitlements would be halted, notably among younger Cubans, boosting prospects of increased non-rationed sales.

A rise in the price of tobacco and alcohol in mid-1994 contributed hugely, especially in the first few months, to putting a squeeze on excess liquidity. But sales of "free" tobacco fell from 16.8 million packs a month in 1994 to 4.5 million in 1996 and authorities are seeking to boost them again, Granma said.
